question_type: Mean monthly yield spread (Aa new corporate minus long-term Treasury) over a 10-year span, read from a stacked multi-year-panel table in a pinned issue whose year labels were lost in OCR

opus_path.decision: Issue pinned to June 1970; series = 'Aa new corporate bonds' minus 'Treasury bonds' (long-term); 120 months Jan 1960-Dec 1969; mean of monthly spreads in percentage points; noted mean of annual means and difference of means give the same number when every year is complete.

Found Table AY-1 'Average Yields of Treasury, Corporate and Municipal Bonds by Periods' in the June 1970 issue; 13 columns = Period + 4 groups x (Treasury, Aa corporate, municipal); 36 monthly rows = 3 stacked blocks of Jan-Dec; last group partially filled (data only through May), so group 4 ends in the publication year.
Recognized that the June 1970 OCR dropped the year-label rows, so the year of each block is unknown from this printing alone.

Recovered year labels from the SAME table in the adjacent May 1970 issue (labels present) and confirmed with July 1970: group1 = first three years starting the year before the range, etc.; used July only for structure because its OCR has digit errors.

Parsed the 36 rows in calc.py, stripping footnote markers glued to some Treasury cells and asserting the month labels cycle Jan..Dec three times; mapped groups to years and kept only 1960-1969 (120 pairs).
Cross-checked all 240 extracted cells against the May 1970 printing: zero mismatches.
Mean of 120 monthly spreads with Decimal arithmetic; confirmed equals mean(corp) - mean(tsy).
Five significant digits; the quotient was exact so no rounding was needed.
Computed and rejected the off-by-one year-block alternative (treating the first block as 1960, i.e. really 1959-1968) and the include-1970 alternative.

opus_key_moves: Noticed the June 1970 printing had lost its year-label rows and did not assume a layout; recovered the labels from the same table in the nearest labeled printing of the same calendar year (May 1970).
Validated the borrowed labels by cell-for-cell value agreement between the two printings (0 mismatches over 240 cells), and used the partially filled last group as a publication-date anchor.
Explicitly computed the off-by-one block mapping as an alternative and rejected it.

none.right_arms_note: Looked up the same table in the April 1970 issue ([40]-[43]), whose header carries the year labels for the first row-block, and applied that mapping to June 1970.

prompt.right_arms_note: Applied the explicit June 1970 block mapping from lesson L-ay1-year-trio-panels at [11]; then caught its own column-index bug ([24]-[25]) because the per-year breakdown at [26] showed implausible negative spreads ([27]) and recomputed at [28].

first_divergence.what_glm_did: Borrowed the year-block layout printed in the February 1971 issue (where the first row-block is labeled with the first year of the range) and applied it unchanged to the June 1970 table ([34], [38]: 'June 1970 table likely columns 1960,1963,1966,1969'). Because the table rolls forward one year each January, this shifted every block by one year, so it averaged Jan 1959-Dec 1968 instead of Jan 1960-Dec 1969.
first_divergence.what_opus_did: Took labels from the same table in the May 1970 issue (same calendar year, so same layout) and verified the mapping by exact cell agreement across the two printings (worklog.md:23-33, 39).
first_divergence.why_glm_went_that_way: Its FTS search at [29] happened to surface a Feb 1971 excerpt with visible year labels; it read that table at [33] and inferred the June 1970 layout from it at [34] with no check that the two printings align. At [34] it even noted that the Feb 1971 first-block January values were ones 'we earlier thought 1961' in June 1970 (a direct sign of a one-year shift) but resolved the conflict in favour of the Feb 1971 labels. Earlier, at [30], its own magnitude reasoning had placed the fourth group's first block in 1968 (consistent with the correct mapping) before it was overridden.
first_divergence.consequence: Year-to-cell mapping off by one year; the submitted mean equals the off-by-one alternative Opus computed and rejected (worklog.md:49); about 12% low.

secondary_errors.note: Its mapping assigned the partially filled last panel (values Jan-May, nan afterwards) to 1971, a year after the June 1970 publication date; this impossible date was waved through ('maybe 1971 not yet'). A feasibility check would have exposed the shift.
Heredoc failures, helper read cap (num_lines > 150) and search cap (limit > 20) errors; cost a few steps but did not cause the error.

saw_correct_evidence.where: [29] search results ranked a labeled April 1970 printing of AY-1 first (it chose the Feb 1971 hit instead); [33] Feb 1971 values that coincide with June 1970's second block (it noticed this at [34]); [30] its own magnitude check matched the correct mapping for the fourth group.

glm_expressed_doubt.where: [20]-[27] and [30] repeatedly unsure which years the blocks hold; no doubt once the Feb 1971 layout was adopted at [34]/[38].

operational.tool_friction: zsh heredoc temp-file failures ([6], [35]); rg not permitted ([3]); helper limits (read <=150 lines [14], search limit <=20 [28]); middle-truncated outputs ([16]-[17]).

adapter_context.relevant_item: none (deck shown was only C003 and C006; no card on AY-1 / stacked year panels / borrowing labels from another vintage)
adapter_context.notes: The prompt arm's context for the same question contained L-ay1-year-trio-panels (learned from sibling ordinal 11 on the same table) with the explicit June 1970 mapping, and that arm got it right; the 16 KB card deck had no equivalent.

remedies.intervention: Cross-vintage alignment check: whenever the actor maps labels/layout from one printing onto another, require that a sample of cells under the proposed mapping (e.g. one full row-block) match between the two printings; return the matching offset if they do not.
remedies.why: Both printings were already on screen ([33], [37]) and the actor noticed a value coincidence at [34] without acting on it; a mechanical match would have returned the one-year offset directly.

remedies.intervention: Date-feasibility check on any period mapping: no mapped period may be after the issue's publication date, and a partially filled panel must be the most recent period.
remedies.why: The cards mapping put partially filled data in a year after the June 1970 publication date ([38]); the check fires on exactly this failure.

remedies.intervention: A 'find labeled printings of this table' lookup that lists other issues carrying the same table title, ranked by publication-date proximity and preferring the same calendar year (rolling tables shift each January).
remedies.why: Opus used May 1970 and the none arm April 1970 (same year) and both were right; the cards arm used Feb 1971 (next year, rolled forward) because an FTS hit surfaced it first.

remedies.intervention: Relevance-retrieved per-table layout memory (e.g. AY-1 year-block mapping per issue range) learned from earlier questions, surfaced when the question names the table/series, instead of a small always-shown card deck.
remedies.why: The prompt arm had exactly this fact (L-ay1-year-trio-panels) and applied it at [11] to get the right mapping; the cards deck had no room for it.

right_arms_note: none: anchored the year blocks with the April 1970 printing (same calendar year, labeled) at [40]-[43]. prompt: used the explicit June 1970 mapping in L-ay1-year-trio-panels at [11], and a per-year breakdown exposed and fixed its own column-index bug at [26]-[28]. Both took labels from a same-year source; cards took them from the next calendar year's rolled-forward printing.
text_vs_mechanism: Text worked here only when it held the specific fact (the prompt arm's AY-1 lesson). A generic text rule such as 'anchor year labels via an adjacent vintage' would not reliably have saved the cards arm, which did anchor via another vintage (the wrong one); a mechanical cross-printing value-alignment check or a date-feasibility check is the robust fix.
notes: Two cheap sanity signals would have caught the cards error: the partial panel landing after the publication date, and per-year spread breakdowns (the prompt arm's per-year printout caught a different bug). Worth making a per-group breakdown plus plausibility review a standard step for flattened multi-panel tables. This question's failure is a single-step selection error, not an operational one.
